symptom: A synthetic caller-owned Proxy can return a valid currentOdds from get while its own data descriptor contains an invalid negative value. The pre-fix validator reads get results, whereas canonical hashing reads descriptors, so validation can accept a digest for different, invalid persisted metadata. A revoked Proxy can also throw before the validator returns a denial. Nested Proxy diagnostic arrays are likewise outside the proven own-data boundary. This is research-only synthetic evidence, not a production incident.
lesson: Own-data descriptor checks are insufficient when the validator reads a caller-controlled Proxy through get and the canonicalizer later reads its descriptors. The validation/hash pair must share a single admitted data authority. Nested Proxy arrays and revoked Proxies must be rejected before consulting caller hooks.
guardrail: For Node-only research ledger ingress, reject root Proxy records and nested diagnostic Proxy arrays using node:util.types.isProxy before Array.isArray, prototype, length, ownKeys, get or descriptor operations. Preserve ordinary records and existing digests. Regress get-versus-descriptor disagreement, revoked root and nested arrays, trap nonexecution and normal digest stability. This does not authenticate external data or permit production connection.
